name: allValue
title: Checks if a value exists / does not exist in each row (column) of a matrix

origin.description: Returns whether every selected element of a vector equals value.
origin.usage: allValue(x, idxs = NULL, value = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector. A matrix is rejected.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

origin.details: When value is logical and x is numeric, zeros are FALSE, non-zero numbers are TRUE, and missing values are NA. That path calls C_rowCounts or C_colCounts with value FALSE and what 0 or 1. Otherwise the value is compared directly. A missing value leaves the result NA until a definite false (for all) or true (for any) is seen.
origin.value: A single logical value, or NA.

translation.description: Returns whether every selected element of a vector equals value.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 1-d numeric or logical vector. A 2-d array is rejected.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based subscripts. None selects every element. A positive index past the end is a missing element.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A single value to search for. A logical value on numeric data treats zeros as FALSE.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm.

translation.details: A logical value on numeric data does not look for 1. It asks the row or column kernel whether any element is zero or whether every element is zero. The result is True, False, or None. None is R's NA. use_names is accepted and does not attach names. The numeric scan is the rowcounts or colcounts crate with what 0 or 1.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowalls import allValue

allValue(np.array([True, True, False]))
